definition: A unit of the International System of Units, built from the seven fundamental units: the kilogram, metre, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.
A word or symbol in front of a unit that multiplies it by a power of ten, such as kilo (k, $10^{3}$) or micro (µ, $10^{-6}$).
A way of writing a number as $a \times 10^{n}$, where $1 \le a < 10$ and $n$ is an integer, as in $3.5 \times 10^{6}$.
The power of ten nearest to a value, used to compare sizes and to quote rough estimates.
The energy gained by one electron accelerated through a potential difference of 1 V, equal to $1.60 \times 10^{-19}$ J.
